subject: Science & Technology
question_text: In the context of the clean energy transition, what are 'Small Modular Reactors' (SMRs)?
options: Miniature fission reactors used exclusively in medical imaging and radioactive tracer synthesis
Advanced nuclear reactors that have a power capacity up to 300 MW(e) per unit and can be factory-fabricated and transported to sites
Fusion-based micro-tokamaks designed for domestic household electricity generation
Mobile solar-powered battery units used for defense installations
explanation: • According to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) are advanced nuclear fission reactors with an electrical power output of up to 300 MW(e) per unit (about one-third of the generating capacity of traditional nuclear power plants). Their modular components can be mass-manufactured in factories and shipped to locations.
standard_book_ref: IAEA Advanced Nuclear Power Reports • Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) Releases
elimination_trap: Fission vs Fusion: SMRs currently being deployed are nuclear FISSION reactors, not fusion reactors.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the role of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) in decarbonizing hard-to-abate industrial sectors and addressing base-load clean energy requirements in India. (10M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text:
With reference to the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, consider the following statements:
1. The temples at Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura were built using fine-grained chloritic schist (soapstone).
2. A signature characteristic of Hoysala temples is the stellate (star-shaped) ground plan raised on a wide platform called 'Jagati'.
3. The temples exclusively venerate Lord Shiva, with no depiction of Vaishnava themes or iconography.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 and 2 are correct: Hoysala artisans utilized soft soapstone (chloritic schist) for intricate filigree carvings, building temples with unique stellate (star-shaped) vimanas set on high Jagati platforms.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Hoysala temples patronized both Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions; the Chennakeshava temple at Belur and Keshava temple at Somanathapura are dedicated to Vishnu (Krishna/Keshava), while Hoysaleshwara at Halebidu is Shaiva.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art, Chapter 6 • Nitin Singhania (Temple Architecture)
elimination_trap: Exclusivity Trap ('exclusively venerate Shiva'): Hoysala rulers were deeply eclectic; Chennakeshava temple at Belur is one of the most famous Vaishnava shrines in India.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze how the Hoysala temple architecture represents a synthesis of Nagara and Dravidian idioms into a distinct Vesara masterpiece. (10M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text: The '30x30 Target', often mentioned in the context of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), refers to:
options: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% below 1990 levels by 2030
Ensuring that at least 30% of degraded terrestrial, inland water, and coastal/marine ecosystems are under effective conservation by 2030
Eliminating 30 hazardous chemical pesticides from agriculture within 30 months
Phasing out 30% of global coal-fired power plants across OECD countries by 2030
explanation: • Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF (adopted at COP15 CBD) commits nations to conserve and protect at least 30% of Earth's lands, inland waters, and ocean areas by 2030 through protected areas and Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs).
standard_book_ref: UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) COP15 • Shankar IAS (Biodiversity)
elimination_trap: Emissions vs Biodiversity: 30x30 is an ecological habitat protection target under CBD, NOT a climate emission reduction target under UNFCCC.

mains_linkage.question: How can India reconcile the 30x30 biodiversity conservation target under the Kunming-Montreal Framework with the community forest rights of indigenous tribal populations under the FRA 2006? (15M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Standing Deposit Facility' (SDF) introduced by the Reserve Bank of India:
1. It enables the RBI to absorb surplus liquidity from commercial banks without providing collateral government securities in return.
2. The SDF rate serves as the lower floor of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor.
3. The introduction of SDF required an amendment to Section 17 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• All statements are correct:
• Statement 1: Unlike reverse repo operations which require collateral G-Secs, SDF allows the central bank to absorb uncollateralized liquidity, preventing collateral shortages during excessive liquidity.
• Statement 2: SDF replaced the fixed reverse repo rate as the floor of the LAF corridor (SDF at policy repo -25 bps; MSF at repo +25 bps).
• Statement 3: An amendment to Section 17 of the RBI Act in 2018 legally empowered the RBI to operationalize SDF.
standard_book_ref: RBI Monetary Policy Framework • Macroeconomics NCERT / Ramesh Singh
elimination_trap: Collateral Requirement: Remember that the primary reason SDF was invented was to absorb liquidity WITHOUT parting with government securities.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the operating architecture of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor and evaluate the efficacy of the Standing Deposit Facility in sterilizing surplus market liquidity. (10M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the Selection Committee responsible for recommending appointments consists of:
1. The Prime Minister of India as Chairperson
2. The Chief Justice of India
3. The Leader of the Opposition or the Leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha
4. A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation:
• Under Section 7(1) of the Act, the Selection Committee consists of: (a) Prime Minister (Chairperson), (b) Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, and (c) a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.
• The Chief Justice of India, who was included by the Supreme Court's interim order in Anoop Baranwal (2023), was replaced by the statutory enactment with a Union Cabinet Minister.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 43 (Election Commission) • CEC & other ECs Act 2023
elimination_trap: CJI Exclusion: The 2023 parliamentary statute explicitly omitted the Chief Justice of India from the Selection Committee, replacing the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister.

mains_linkage.question: Examine whether the exclusion of the Chief Justice of India from the Selection Committee for Election Commissioners dilutes the institutional autonomy envisioned under Article 324. (15M)

subject: Geography
question_text:
With reference to Lithium exploration in India, consider the following statements:
1. Salal-Haimana in the Reasi district of Jammu & Kashmir and Katghora in Chhattisgarh have been identified as major lithium-bearing blocks.
2. The Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act permits the auction of critical and strategic minerals to private sector companies.
3. India is currently the world's largest producer of refined lithium, surpassing Chile and Australia.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 and 2 are correct: GSI discovered lithium inferred resources in Reasi (J&K) and Katghora (Chhattisgarh). Legislative amendments in MMDR and OAMDR allowed commercial auction of 24 critical/strategic minerals including lithium to private players.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Australia is the largest lithium producer and Chile has the largest reserves, while China dominates refining (>60%). India is currently an import-dependent country for processed lithium.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Mines Annual Report • Indian Minerals Yearbook
elimination_trap: Global Leader Trap: India has newly discovered deposits, but is far from being the largest producer or refiner.

mains_linkage.question: Critical minerals are the bedrock of the 21st-century clean energy transition. Examine India's domestic exploration and overseas acquisition strategies through KABIL. (10M)

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Post-Quantum Cryptography' (PQC):
1. It refers to cryptographic algorithms designed to secure digital communications against decryption attacks by future quantum computers.
2. Most existing public-key encryption standards like RSA and ECC are theoretically vulnerable to Shor's algorithm running on a sufficiently powerful quantum computer.
3. PQC algorithms can only be executed on quantum processors and cannot run on traditional classical silicon computers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 and 2 are correct: Quantum algorithms like Shor's algorithm can solve prime factorization and discrete logarithms in polynomial time, breaking RSA and ECC encryption. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) develops mathematical problems (lattice-based, code-based) that quantum computers cannot easily solve.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: A crucial feature of PQC is that it runs on EXISTING classical computers and standard internet hardware; it does NOT require a quantum computer to operate.
standard_book_ref: National Quantum Mission (NQM) Compendium • NIST PQC Standards
elimination_trap: Hardware Trap: Post-Quantum Cryptography is designed to run on ordinary CLASSICAL computers to protect them against quantum attacks.

mains_linkage.question: The advent of quantum computing poses asymmetric threats to modern cybersecurity and sovereign data infrastructure. How does the National Quantum Mission address this vulnerability? (15M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
The 'High Seas Treaty' (Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction - BBNJ Agreement) recently signed under UNCLOS focuses on:
1. Establishing Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in international waters outside Exclusive Economic Zones.
2. Fair and equitable sharing of benefits derived from Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs).
3. Granting exclusive territorial sovereignty over mineral-rich seabed polymetallic nodule fields to coastal developing states.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The BBNJ Treaty creates an international legal framework to establish MPAs in areas beyond national jurisdiction (covering nearly two-thirds of the world's oceans) and mandates transparent benefit-sharing from marine genetic resources.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: The High Seas and the international seabed ('The Area') are designated as the 'Common Heritage of Humankind'. No state can claim or exercise sovereignty over any part thereof (governed by the International Seabed Authority).
standard_book_ref: UNCLOS III Framework • Shankar IAS Environment (Marine Ecosystems)
elimination_trap: Sovereignty Distractor: High Seas are open to all and belong to no single sovereign; mineral exploitation in 'The Area' is regulated by ISA as Common Heritage of Mankind.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the strategic and environmental significance of the BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) for global ocean conservation and India's Deep Ocean Mission. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
With reference to the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) notified under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) acts as the administrator for the Indian carbon market.
2. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) is the regulator for trading of Carbon Credit Certificates.
3. Only voluntary non-obligated entities can trade carbon credits, whereas obligated energy-intensive industries are excluded from the domestic market.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) is the statutory administrator recommending targets and issuing Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs).
• Statement 2 is correct: CERC is mandated as the regulator for trading of carbon credits across recognized power exchanges.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: The scheme has a mandatory compliance mechanism for designated obligated energy-intensive sectors (fertilizers, steel, cement) as well as an offset mechanism for voluntary non-obligated entities.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Power CCTS Framework • Ramesh Singh / Economic Survey
elimination_trap: Exclusive Exclusion Trap ('only voluntary entities'): National carbon trading regimes rely fundamentally on mandatory compliance caps on heavy industrial emitters.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the institutional architecture of the Indian Carbon Market (ICM) and assess its potential to incentivize industrial decarbonization without hurting manufacturing competitiveness. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam), consider the following statements:
1. It reserves one-third of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha, the State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
2. The reservation comes into effect immediately without requiring any delimitation exercise or post-amendment census publication.
3. The horizontal reservation for women shall continue in perpetuity unless expressly abolished by a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: The 106th CAA, 2023 inserted Articles 330A, 332A, and 239AA(2)(b) reserving 33% seats for women in Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and NCT of Delhi.
• Statement 2 is incorrect: Under newly inserted Article 334A, the reservation takes effect only after an exercise of delimitation is undertaken based on the relevant figures of the first census conducted after the commencement of the Act.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 334A(1), the sunset clause provides that the reservation shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of 15 years from its commencement (unless extended by Parliament by law).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 22 (Parliament) & Constitutional Amendments Summary • Articles 330A, 332A & 334A
elimination_trap: Immediate Implementation Trap: The 106th CAA explicitly conditions operationalization on the post-enactment census and subsequent delimitation.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the constitutional design and socio-political hurdles in operationalizing the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act for women's legislative representation. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Union Executive in India, consider the following statements:
1. The President of India summons, prorogues and dissolves each House of Parliament on the advice of the Prime Minister.
2. The Constitution of India provides that the President shall act in accordance with the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head.
3. The President cannot ask the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The President summons and prorogues both Houses on the advice of the Council of Ministers (Cabinet), not solely the Prime Minister alone.
• Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 74(1), there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Under the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 (proviso to Article 74(1)), the President MAY require the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice once.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 17 (President) • Article 74(1) & 44th CAA 1978
elimination_trap: Absolute Word Trap ('cannot'): Proviso to Article 74 explicitly allows one-time reconsideration.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the scope of presidential discretion under Article 74 of the Indian Constitution with judicial precedents. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
With reference to Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) or Digital Rupee (e₹) launched by the Reserve Bank of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is a sovereign currency issued by the RBI in alignment with monetary policy.
2. It appears as a liability on the RBI's balance sheet just like physical banknotes.
3. It cannot be converted into commercial bank deposits or physical cash.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: CBDC is a legal tender issued by the central bank in digital form, representing sovereign fiat currency.
• Statement 2 is correct: Just like physical cash, digital currency is a direct claim on the central bank and forms part of reserve money (M0), appearing as a liability on the RBI's balance sheet.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: CBDC is 100% fungible and convertible at par (1:1) into physical banknotes and commercial bank deposits.
standard_book_ref: RBI Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) • Macroeconomics NCERT Class 12
elimination_trap: Negative Inversion Trap ('cannot be converted'): Sovereign digital currencies must maintain 1:1 convertibility with cash.

mains_linkage.question: How will Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) transform cross-border remittances and domestic monetary transmission in India? (15M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
Consider the following Ramsar Wetlands in India:
1. Bhoj Wetland
2. Renuka Wetland
3. Rudrasagar Lake
4. Sasthamkotta Lake

How many of the above are correctly matched with their respective states?
• Bhoj Wetland : Madhya Pradesh
• Renuka Wetland : Himachal Pradesh
• Rudrasagar Lake : Tripura
• Sasthamkotta Lake : Kerala
explanation:
• Bhoj Wetland is in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh (formed by Upper and Lower Lakes).
• Renuka Wetland is in Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh (smallest Ramsar site in India).
• Rudrasagar Lake is in Melaghar, Tripura.
• Sasthamkotta Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Kerala (Kollam district).
All 4 pairs are correctly matched.
standard_book_ref: MoEFCC Ramsar Sites Directory • Shankar IAS Environment (Aquatic Ecosystems)
elimination_trap: Pair Format: You cannot eliminate options by picking A/B; each individual state match must be verified.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the efficacy of the Amrit Dharohar initiative in rejuvenating Ramsar sites across India while supporting local livelihoods. (10M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text: In medieval India, the term 'Fanam' referred to which of the following?
explanation:
• 'Fanam' (or Panam) was a small gold or silver coin historically minted in South India, especially during the Vijayanagara Empire, Nayakas, Travancore, and Mysore kingdoms.
• It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Pana' (a monetary denomination used since the Mauryan period).
standard_book_ref: Satish Chandra, Medieval India (Trade & Currency under Vijayanagara) • NCERT Class 7 Themes in Indian History
elimination_trap: Obscure Terminology: In ancient and medieval questions, terms ending in '-nam' or '-panam' in South India almost always relate to currency/taxation (Panam = Money).

mains_linkage.question: Monetary monetization and urban market centers were the cornerstone of Vijayanagara's imperial prosperity. Elucidate with contemporary traveler accounts. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Election Commission of India:
1. The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners enjoy equal powers but receive unequal salaries.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner is entitled to the same salary as is provided to a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. The recommendations of the Chief Election Commissioner are mandatory for removing an Election Commissioner from office.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The CEC and other ECs have equal powers, receive equal salary, allowances and perquisites similar to a Supreme Court Judge.
• Statement 2 is correct: Under the Election Commission (Conditions of Service) Act, the CEC receives salary equal to that of a Supreme Court Judge.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner can only be removed upon the recommendation of the CEC; however, the Supreme Court has clarified that the President is not bound to accept it if it is arbitrary (the recommendation is a constitutional safeguard, but not termed 'mandatory' executive dictate).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 43 (Election Commission) • Article 324(5)
elimination_trap: Unequal Salary Myth: UPSC frequently tests whether CEC has higher salary than other ECs (they are completely equal).

mains_linkage.question: Examine the tension between the right to contest elections and the need to uphold electoral ethics under the Representation of the People Act. (15M)

subject: Geography
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding Earthquake waves:
1. P-waves are longitudinal waves that can travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid materials.
2. S-waves are transverse waves that cannot pass through liquids.
3. The shadow zone of S-waves is significantly smaller than the shadow zone of P-waves.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: Primary (P) waves are compressional/longitudinal waves; particle motion is parallel to wave propagation. They travel through solids, liquids, and gases.
• Statement 2 is correct: Secondary (S) waves are shear/transverse waves; they can only travel through solid materials and are blocked by Earth's liquid outer core.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: The shadow zone of S-waves is MUCH LARGER than P-waves (S-waves do not appear anywhere beyond 105° from epicenter, covering over 40% of the earth's surface, whereas P-waves shadow zone is only between 105° and 145°).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Chapter 3 (Interior of the Earth)
elimination_trap: Inversion Trap: S-wave shadow zone is massive (>40% of Earth), while P-wave shadow zone is a narrow band (105°-145°).

mains_linkage.question: Explain the mechanism of earthquake genesis and elucidate why the Pacific Ring of Fire exhibits intense seismic and volcanic activity. (15M)

subject: Economy
question_text: In India, which one of the following is responsible for maintaining price stability by controlling inflation?
explanation:
• Under the RBI Act, 1934 (amended in 2016 via the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement), the primary objective of the Reserve Bank of India is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is statutorily mandated to target CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics • Section 45ZB of RBI Act, 1934
elimination_trap: FSDC distractor: FSDC handles inter-regulatory coordination, not statutory inflation targeting.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the institutional mechanism of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in balancing inflation management with economic growth impulses. (10M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text: The 'Miyawaki method' is well known for the:
options: Promotion of commercial farming in arid and semi-arid areas
Development of urban forests using native plant species in compact urban spaces
Harvesting of wind energy on coastal boundaries
Cultivation of genetically modified food crops in floodplains
explanation:
• Pioneered by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, the Miyawaki technique involves planting 2 to 4 native species of trees per square meter in dense mini-groves.
• It enables trees to grow up to 10 times faster and creates dense urban micro-forests within 20–30 years instead of 200–300 years, boosting local biodiversity and lowering urban heat island effects.
standard_book_ref: Down to Earth Magazine / Current Affairs Compendiums • Urban Forestry Guidelines MoEFCC
elimination_trap: Farming vs Forestry: Miyawaki is purely an ecological native reforestation technique, never commercial monoculture farming.

mains_linkage.question: Urban Heat Islands (UHIs) represent a growing ecological vulnerability in Indian metros. How can urban afforestation methods like Miyawaki mitigate microclimate distress? (10M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text: A legislation which confers on the executive or administrative authority an unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power in the matter of the application of law violates which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
explanation:
• In Maneka Gandhi (1978) and E.P. Royappa (1974), the Supreme Court ruled that Article 14 strikes at arbitrariness in state action. Equality and arbitrariness are sworn enemies.
• Any law conferring unguided, uncanalized, and uncontrolled discretionary power upon the executive without statutory standards violates Article 14 (Rule of Law & Non-Arbitrariness).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 7 (Fundamental Rights - Article 14) • E.P. Royappa Case Precedent
elimination_trap: Article 32 distractor: Article 32 is the remedy to enforce rights, but the substantive right against arbitrariness itself is anchored in Article 14.

mains_linkage.question: Arbitrariness in administrative discretion is the antithesis of the Rule of Law. Discuss how the doctrine of non-arbitrariness under Article 14 limits executive overreach. (15M)

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
With reference to CRISPR-Cas9 technology, consider the following statements:
1. It is a molecular tool used by scientists to edit parts of the genome by removing, adding, or altering sections of DNA sequence.
2. The Cas9 protein acts as a pair of molecular scissors that cuts the two strands of DNA at a specific location in the genome.
3. It cannot be used to treat genetic disorders in human germline cells.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: CRISPR-Cas9 allows precise, targeted editing of DNA sequences across organisms.
• Statement 2 is correct: Cas9 is an endonuclease enzyme ('molecular scissors') guided by a synthetic guide RNA (gRNA) to make double-stranded cuts at targeted genomic loci.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: CRISPR-Cas9 CAN technically be used in human germline cells (embryos, eggs, sperm), though it is heavily regulated or ethically banned in many jurisdictions. The question states 'cannot be used', which is technically false (as seen in the He Jiankui CCR5 gene-editing case).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Biology (Biotechnology: Principles & Processes) • Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020
elimination_trap: Technical Capability vs Ethical Ban: Never confuse 'legally restricted' with 'scientifically impossible'.

mains_linkage.question: What are the ethical dilemmas and biosecurity concerns associated with human germline gene editing using CRISPR-Cas9? (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
In the context of the Indian economy, which of the following are categorized as 'Capital Goods'?
1. Tools, machinery and factory equipment used in manufacturing
2. Raw materials consumed in the production process
3. Transport vehicles used in commercial logistics

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation:
• Statement 1 and 3 are correct: Capital goods are durable tangible assets (machinery, tools, commercial trucks) used repeatedly over years to produce other goods and services.
• Statement 2 is incorrect: Raw materials are 'Intermediate Goods' (consumed completely in a single production cycle), not capital goods.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics, Chapter 2 (National Income Accounting) • Ramesh Singh (Capital Formation)
elimination_trap: Intermediate vs Capital Trap: Raw materials are intermediate single-use inputs, not durable fixed capital.

mains_linkage.question: Examine how gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) in infrastructure crowd-in private investments and accelerates long-term GDP growth. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker exercises a casting vote only in the case of an equality of votes in the first instance.
2. When a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker can neither preside nor vote in any proceeding.
3. A Speaker vacating office resigns by submitting the resignation letter in writing addressed to the President of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 100(1), the Speaker does not vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote in the case of equality of votes.
• Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Article 96(2), when a removal resolution is under consideration, the Speaker cannot preside, but HAS THE RIGHT TO VOTE in the first instance (though not in the case of an equality of votes).
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 94(b), the Speaker resigns by writing to the DEPUTY SPEAKER of the Lok Sabha, not the President.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 22 (Parliament - Presiding Officers) • Articles 94, 96 & 100
elimination_trap: Resignation Recipient Trap: Speaker resigns to Deputy Speaker, NOT the President (unlike Supreme Court judges or Ministers).

mains_linkage.question: The impartiality of the Speaker's office has faced constitutional scrutiny in disqualification petitions under the Tenth Schedule. Critically analyze. (15M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to the Project Cheetah in India, consider the following statements:
1. Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in the year 1952.
2. The cheetahs reintroduced into Kuno National Park were translocated from Namibia and South Africa, which belong to the Asiatic cheetah sub-species.
3. The Asiatic cheetah is currently classified as 'Critically Endangered' by the IUCN, with its only surviving wild population in Iran.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Asiatic cheetah was officially declared extinct in India in 1952 after the last three individuals were shot in 1947 in Surguja (Chhattisgarh).
• Statement 2 is incorrect: The cheetahs translocated from Namibia and South Africa are AFRICAN cheetahs (Acinonyx jubatus jubatus), not Asiatic cheetahs.
• Statement 3 is correct: The Asiatic cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus venaticus) is Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, surviving only in Iran (<50 individuals).
standard_book_ref: MoEFCC Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India • Shankar IAS (Biodiversity)
elimination_trap: Subspecies Swap Trap: Reintroduced cheetahs are African cheetahs (Vulnerable), while Asiatic cheetahs survive only in Iran (Critically Endangered).

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the ecological and management challenges of intercontinental mega-carnivore translocations in India in light of Project Cheetah. (10M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text: In the context of ancient Tamil literature, what is 'Tolkappiyam' primarily celebrated as?
options: An epic poem narrating the tragic story of Kovalan and Kannagi
A comprehensive treatise on Tamil grammar and poetic conventions, with reflections on socio-political life
A Buddhist philosophical treatise on ethics and logic
A manual on irrigation engineering and maritime shipbuilding under the Cholas
explanation:
• Tolkappiyam, authored by Tolkappiyar, is the earliest extant work of Tamil literature.
• It is divided into three sections (Eluttu, Col, Porul): while the first two deal with phonology and morphology/grammar, the third section (Porulatikaram) provides rich insights into the 'Tinai' (five physiographic landscapes), marital customs, warfare, and socio-economic life.
standard_book_ref: Upinder Singh, History of Ancient and Early Medieval India, Chapter 8 • NCERT Class 11
elimination_trap: Silappadikaram Distractor: Kovalan and Kannagi is the subject of Silappadikaram (by Ilango Adigal), NOT Tolkappiyam.

mains_linkage.question: Sangam literature serves as an invaluable window into the agrarian transitions, tribal institutions, and maritime trade of early historic South India. Discuss. (15M)

subject: Geography
question_text:
Consider the following minerals found in the beach sands of coastal India:
1. Ilmenite
2. Rutile
3. Monazite
4. Zircon

Which of the above are sources of Titanium?
explanation:
• Ilmenite (FeTiO3) and Rutile (TiO2) are the primary commercial ore sources for Titanium metal and titanium dioxide pigment.
• Monazite is a phosphate mineral containing rare earths and Thorium.
• Zircon is a zirconium silicate (source of Zirconium metal used in nuclear fuel cladding).
standard_book_ref: Indian Minerals Yearbook (Indian Bureau of Mines) • NCERT Class 12 India: People and Economy
elimination_trap: Mineral Association: Beach sands contain Ilmenite, Rutile, Zircon, and Monazite together, but ONLY Ilmenite and Rutile yield Titanium.

mains_linkage.question: Assess the strategic importance of critical and beach sand minerals for India's clean energy transition and high-technology manufacturing. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER):
1. An increase in India's REER indicates an appreciation in the currency's external trade competitiveness.
2. An increase in the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates an appreciation of the Rupee against a basket of currencies.
3. An increasing divergence between NEER and REER highlights divergent domestic and foreign inflation rates.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: An increase (appreciation) in India's REER means Indian exports become more expensive relative to trading partners, indicating a LOSS of trade competitiveness.
• Statement 2 is correct: NEER is the weighted average of bilateral nominal exchange rates; an increase means nominal currency appreciation.
• Statement 3 is correct: Since REER adjusts NEER for relative price differentials (inflation differential), a widening gap reflects differences in inflation rates between India and trading partners.
standard_book_ref: Macroeconomics NCERT Class 12, Chapter 6 (Open Economy Macroeconomics) • RBI Bulletin
elimination_trap: Currency Appreciation vs Competitiveness: Currency appreciation HARMS price competitiveness of exports; it does not improve it.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the divergence between NEER and REER in emerging markets and discuss how exchange rate volatility impacts export basket diversification. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text: In the Indian Constitutional jurisprudence, the concept of 'Due Process of Law' entails which of the following?
options: Strict compliance with procedure established by statutory law
Fair, just and reasonable application of the law protecting natural justice
The sovereign power of the legislature to enact retrospective penal laws
The supremacy of customary practices over statutory enactments
explanation: • In Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court held that the 'procedure established by law' under Article 21 cannot be arbitrary, oppressive, or fanciful; it must be 'right, just and fair', effectively reading American substantive 'Due Process of Law' into Article 21.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 7 (Fundamental Rights - Protection of Life and Personal Liberty) • Maneka Gandhi (1978)
elimination_trap: Literal Text vs Judicial Interpretation: The text of Article 21 says 'procedure established by law', but since 1978, the doctrine applied is substantive fairness (natural justice).

mains_linkage.question: Trace the transition from A.K. Gopalan to Maneka Gandhi in the interpretation of Article 21. How has substantive due process enriched fundamental rights? (10M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol:
1. It aims for the global phase-down of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).
2. HFCs are potent ozone-depleting substances that directly destroy the stratospheric ozone layer.
3. The Kigali Amendment legally binds member countries to timeline targets for phasing down HFC consumption.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Kigali Amendment (entered into force 2019) mandates gradual phase-down of HFCs.
• Statement 2 is incorrect: HFCs do NOT deplete the ozone layer (they have zero ODP - Ozone Depletion Potential), but they are powerful greenhouse gases with high Global Warming Potential (GWP).
• Statement 3 is correct: The Kigali Amendment is legally binding under international environmental law.
standard_book_ref: Shankar IAS Environment (Ozone Depletion & Climate Agreements) • UNEP Ozone Secretariat
elimination_trap: ODS vs GHG Trap: HFCs replaced CFCs precisely because HFCs do NOT destroy ozone; they are targeted now because they accelerate global warming.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze the implications of the Kigali Amendment for India's cooling and refrigeration manufacturing sector under the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP). (15M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text: In ancient India, which one of the following places was a prominent Buddhist center that flourished under the Mahasanghikas and was known as 'Dhanyakataka'?
explanation: • Dhanyakataka (modern Dharanikota near Amaravati in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh) was the capital of the Satavahanas and a renowned mahachaitya center of the Mahasanghika school of Buddhism.
standard_book_ref: Upinder Singh, Ancient India • NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art, Chapter 4
elimination_trap: Nagarjunakonda Distractor: While nearby Nagarjunakonda is also an Ikshvaku Buddhist site, historical Dhanyakataka refers strictly to Amaravati.

mains_linkage.question: Highlight the distinctive architectural and sculptural features of the Amaravati school of art and contrast it with Mathura sculpture. (10M)

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding Ballistic and Cruise Missiles:
1. Cruise missiles are jet-propelled and fly entirely within the earth's atmosphere at constant aerodynamic lift.
2. Ballistic missiles leave the earth's atmosphere during part of their flight trajectory and re-enter following a sub-orbital parabolic path.
3. Agni-V is an intercontinental cruise missile, whereas BrahMos is a supersonic ballistic missile.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is correct: Cruise missiles are unmanned self-propelled guided vehicles flying within the atmosphere at low altitudes.
• Statement 2 is correct: Ballistic missiles are rocket-propelled during the initial launch phase, arc into space, and follow a gravitational ballistic trajectory back to the target.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Agni-V is a long-range BALLISTIC missile, while BrahMos is a supersonic CRUISE missile (missile types are inverted).
standard_book_ref: DRDO Technology Focus • Science & Technology Compendiums
elimination_trap: Pair Inversion: Agni is ballistic, BrahMos is cruise. UPSC frequently swaps names of prominent defense systems.

mains_linkage.question: How has the induction of supersonic and hypersonic cruise missiles transformed India's maritime and anti-access/area-denial (A2/AD) capabilities? (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, consider the following statements:
1. The power of the Supreme Court and High Courts to punish for contempt is derived exclusively from the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.
2. The Constitution of India defines both 'Civil Contempt' and 'Criminal Contempt'.
3. In India, the Parliament is vested with the power to make laws regarding contempt of court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The Supreme Court and High Courts derive their contempt powers directly from the Constitution (Articles 129 and 215 as Courts of Record), which cannot be abridged even by parliamentary statute.
• Statement 2 is incorrect: The Constitution DOES NOT define civil or criminal contempt; they are defined in Section 2 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.
• Statement 3 is correct: Parliament has the constitutional authority under Entry 77 of the Union List and Entry 14 of the Concurrent List to legislate on contempt of court.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 26 (Supreme Court) • Articles 129, 215 & Contempt of Courts Act 1971
elimination_trap: Constitutional Definition Trap: The Constitution mentions 'contempt of court', but NEVER defines what constitutes civil or criminal contempt.

mains_linkage.question: Does the law of criminal contempt under the Contempt of Courts Act 1971 chill legitimate public scrutiny of the judiciary? Analyze with recent judgments. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text: In the context of the Indian economy, 'Open Market Operations' (OMO) conducted by the Reserve Bank of India refer to the:
options: Borrowing by scheduled commercial banks from the RBI against collateral
Purchase and sale of government securities by the central bank in the open market
Lending by commercial banks to priority sectors at subsidized interest rates
Fixation of statutory minimum export prices for agricultural commodities
explanation: • Open Market Operations (OMOs) involve the outright purchase and sale of government securities (G-Secs) by the RBI to adjust the rupee liquidity conditions in the financial system on a durable basis.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics • RBI Functions & Working
elimination_trap: Repo vs OMO: Short-term collateralized borrowing is Repo/Reverse Repo, whereas outright sale/purchase of G-Secs is OMO.

mains_linkage.question: Explain how Open Market Operations (OMOs) and Operation Twist help the central bank manage sovereign yield curves and macroeconomic liquidity. (10M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text: The term 'Biorock Technology' is frequently discussed in the media in the context of which of the following?
options: Extraction of shale gas from offshore geological formations
Restoration and regeneration of damaged coral reefs and marine habitats
Stabilization of agricultural soil slopes in landslide-prone hill areas
In situ remediation of heavy metals from municipal wastewater
explanation: • Biorock (mineral accretion technology) passes low-voltage electrical currents through seawater to precipitate calcium carbonate onto steel structures, accelerating coral calcification up to 3 to 5 times faster than normal.
standard_book_ref: Zoological Survey of India (Coral Restoration in Gulf of Kutch) • PMF IAS Environment
elimination_trap: Shale Gas Distractor: 'Rock' implies geological mining, but 'Bio-rock' is an electro-chemical marine calcification technique for corals.

mains_linkage.question: Ocean acidification and marine heatwaves are triggering unprecedented coral bleaching. Evaluate technological interventions like Biorock in preserving marine biodiversity. (15M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Ashokan sites and their corresponding Indian States:
1. Dhauli : Odisha
2. Erragudi : Andhra Pradesh
3. Jaugada : Madhya Pradesh
4. Kalsi : Karnataka

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation:
• Dhauli is in Odisha (near Bhubaneswar, site of Kalinga War) — Correct.
• Erragudi is in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh — Correct.
• Jaugada is in Ganjam district of ODISHA (not Madhya Pradesh) — Incorrect.
• Kalsi is in Dehradun district of UTTARAKHAND (not Karnataka) — Incorrect.
Therefore, exactly two pairs are correctly matched.
standard_book_ref: Upinder Singh, Chapter 7 (The Mauryan Empire) • Archaeological Survey of India Edict Inventory
elimination_trap: Pair Format: Kalsi is in the North (Uttarakhand hills) and Jaugada is in coastal Odisha. Only two pairs are valid.

mains_linkage.question: Ashokan edicts were an innovative medium for imperial communication and moral cohesion across diverse linguistic zones. Discuss. (10M)

subject: Geography
question_text: The 'Gandikota canyon' of South India was carved out by which one of the following rivers?
explanation: • Known as the 'Grand Canyon of India', the Gandikota gorge was cut through the Erramala hills in Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh by the Pennar River over millions of years.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 11 Physical Geography • Survey of India Geotourism Sites
elimination_trap: Tungabhadra Distractor: Hampi gorge is associated with Tungabhadra, whereas the dramatic Gandikota red granite canyon belongs strictly to Pennar.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the geomorphological processes responsible for canyon and gorge formation and how river rejuvenation shapes peninsular valleys. (10M)

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
With reference to 'Web 3.0', consider the following statements:
1. Web 3.0 technology enables people to control their own personal data without reliance on centralized server platforms.
2. In Web 3.0, blockchain-based social networks and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) can operate.
3. Web 3.0 operates primarily by replacing public internet infrastructure with closed private fiber-optic channels.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Web 3.0 represents a decentralized, permissionless web where users retain data ownership through cryptography and smart contracts without centralized tech monopolies.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: Web 3.0 runs on standard open internet protocols and distributed peer-to-peer networks, not closed private cables.
standard_book_ref: Science & Technology Current Affairs Compendiums • IEEE Tech Reports
elimination_trap: Physical vs Protocol Layer: Web 3.0 is a decentralized software application/protocol layer, not proprietary private hardware cables.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the potential of Web 3.0 and Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) in enhancing data sovereignty and algorithmic transparency. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text: A 'Constitutional Government' by definition is a:
explanation: • The essence of constitutionalism is 'Limited Government'. A constitution imposes institutional checks and balances, separation of powers, and fundamental rights to restrict arbitrary state authority and prevent majoritarian tyranny.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 11 Indian Constitution at Work, Chapter 1 • M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 3
elimination_trap: Democracy vs Constitutionalism: A government can be 'popular' or 'multi-party' but still act arbitrarily; a constitutional government is fundamentally one with legal limitations on power.

mains_linkage.question: Constitutionalism is not merely having a written constitution; it requires an ethos of restraint and institutional vigilance. Elaborate. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text: The 'Money Multiplier' in an economy increases with which one of the following?
options: Increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in the banks
Increase in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in the banks
Increase in the banking habits of the population
Increase in the population of the country
explanation:
• Money Multiplier equals Broad Money (M3) divided by Reserve Money (M0). When people hold less currency in cash and deposit more money into banks (increasing banking habits), banks have more deposits to create credit, expanding the money multiplier.
• Increasing CRR or SLR forces banks to hold more reserves, which REDUCES credit creation and lowers the multiplier.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics, Chapter 3 (Money and Banking)
elimination_trap: Reserve Ratio Inversion: Higher CRR decreases the money multiplier ($m = 1/r$). Greater banking habits increases it.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze the role of digital public infrastructure (UPI, Jan Dhan accounts) in formalizing household savings and increasing monetary transmission. (15M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text: What is 'Blue Carbon'?
options: Carbon captured by coastal, aquatic and marine ecosystems
Carbon sequestered in deep permafrost and polar ice caps
Carbon emissions produced from offshore oil and petroleum drilling
Carbon captured directly from industrial chimneys into synthetic polymers
explanation: • 'Blue Carbon' refers to the carbon captured and sequestered by the world's oceanic and coastal ecosystems, primarily mangroves, tidal salt marshes, and seagrass meadows. These habitats sequester carbon up to 10 times faster per hectare than terrestrial tropical rainforests.
standard_book_ref: UNEP Blue Carbon Policy Report • Shankar IAS (Aquatic Ecosystems)
elimination_trap: Direct Concept: Blue stands for marine/oceanic ecosystems, Green for terrestrial forests, Brown/Black for fossil fuels and industrial soot.

mains_linkage.question: Assess the potential of coastal blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, seagrasses) in India's strategy to achieve Net Zero by 2070. (10M)

subject: History & Culture
question_text: With reference to 8th August 1942 in Indian history, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The Quit India Resolution was adopted by the All India Congress Committee at Bombay
The Viceroy's Executive Council was expanded to include more Indians under the August Offer
The Congress ministries resigned in seven provinces protesting World War II
Cripps Mission arrived in New Delhi proposing Dominion status post-war
explanation: • On 8 August 1942, the All India Congress Committee passed the historic 'Quit India' Resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, where Mahatma Gandhi delivered his famous 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) speech.
standard_book_ref: Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence • Rajiv Ahir (Spectrum Modern India)
elimination_trap: August Offer vs Quit India: August Offer was 8 August 1940; Quit India was 8 August 1942.

mains_linkage.question: The Quit India Movement of 1942 was characterized by unprecedented underground networks and parallel governments (Prati Sarkar). Elaborate. (15M)

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text: What is the legal status of the 'Right to Property' in India today?
options: Fundamental Right available to citizens only
Legal right available to citizens only
Legal right available to any person
Neither Fundamental Right nor legal right
explanation:
• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 repealed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, stripping property of its Fundamental Right status.
• It inserted Article 300A in Part XII: 'No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law'. It is a constitutional/legal right available to 'any person' (citizens as well as non-citizens and corporate entities).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Chapter 7 & Chapter 34 (Property Rights - Article 300A)
elimination_trap: Citizen vs Any Person Trap: Article 300A uses the word 'person', not 'citizen'. Therefore, foreign nationals and juristic entities also enjoy legal protection against unlawful confiscation.

mains_linkage.question: Examine how the Supreme Court has interpreted Article 300A to ensure fair compensation and human dignity in compulsory land acquisitions. (10M)

subject: Economy
question_text:
If the RBI decides to adopt an 'Expansionary Monetary Policy', which of the following would it NOT do?
1. Cut and optimize the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
2. Increase the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate
3. Cut the Bank Rate and Repo Rate

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation:
• In an expansionary (easy money) policy, the RBI wants to stimulate credit growth by lowering interest rates (cutting Repo Rate, Bank Rate, MSF rate) and lowering reserve requirements (cutting SLR/CRR).
• Increasing the MSF rate makes overnight borrowing expensive for banks, which is a CONTRACTIONARY measure. Hence, RBI would NOT increase MSF rate.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics • Ramesh Singh (Monetary Policy Tools)
elimination_trap: Negative Question Trap ('would it NOT do'): The question asks what the RBI avoids doing during stimulus. Increasing MSF suppresses liquidity.

mains_linkage.question: Assess the effectiveness of counter-cyclical monetary policy versus targeted fiscal support during macroeconomic stagflation. (15M)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text: Which one of the following has been constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
explanation:
• The Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) was constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 pursuant to the Supreme Court's directives in M.C. Mehta vs Union of India.
• CGWB, on the other hand, is a subordinate office under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
standard_book_ref: MoEFCC Acts & Rules • Shankar IAS (Environmental Institutions)
elimination_trap: Board vs Authority: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) is an administrative body formed in 1970; Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) is the statutory body under EPA 1986.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze the governance deficit in groundwater regulation in India and assess the statutory enforcement powers of the Central Ground Water Authority. (10M)

subject: Geography
question_text: Siachen Glacier is situated to the:
explanation:
• Siachen Glacier lies in the Eastern Karakoram range immediately North of the Nubra Valley. Meltwater from Siachen Glacier feeds the Nubra River, which flows into the Shyok River and subsequently into the Indus River system.
• It lies West of Aksai Chin, North of Leh, and East of Gilgit.
standard_book_ref: Oxford School Atlas / Orient BlackSwan • NCERT Class 11 India: Physical Environment
elimination_trap: Directional Compass: Siachen is West of Aksai Chin (not East) and North of Nubra Valley.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the strategic and geopolitical significance of the Siachen-Saltoro complex in guarding India's northern frontiers. (10M)

subject: Science & Technology
question_text: In the context of recent developments in medical science, what is 'Pronuclear Transfer' used for?
options: Deterrence of biodegradation of agricultural produce
Development of biodegradable plastics from marine algae
Production of synthetic hormones using genetically modified yeasts
Prevention of mitochondrial diseases in offspring
explanation:
• Pronuclear transfer (PNT) is an in vitro fertilization (IVF) technique used in mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT).
• It transfers the pronuclei from a fertilized egg containing faulty maternal mitochondrial DNA into an enucleated healthy donor egg with normal mitochondria, preventing severe inherited mitochondrial disorders in the baby (often popularized as 'three-parent IVF').
standard_book_ref: The Lancet / Nature Biotech Reports • NCERT Biology Class 12
elimination_trap: Nuclear vs Mitochondrial: PNT cures mitochondrial DNA defects (inherited exclusively maternally), not nuclear chromosome defects.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the scientific mechanism and ethical dilemmas associated with mitochondrial replacement therapy (three-parent baby technology). (10M)
